newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares fall, seen drifting sideways.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares fall, seen drifting sideways.

text.p: The Slovenian blue-chip SBI share index fell 3.30 percent on Tuesday on what traders said was profit-taking combined with selling from small shareholders prior to the summer holidays.
The SBI index fell 3.30 percent or 47.62 points to 1,396.68. Market participants forecast that the market would drift sideways for the rest of the week.

"A downward correction was certainly needed, it seems like foreign investors will start buying more considerately. People are also selling to get money for their summer holiday," said Ales Novak, a trader at brokers Ilirika.
He added that the SBI index was likely to rise by about 10 percent until the end of the summer if the current optimistic mood lasts.
Overall 12 shares fell, three rose and two were flat while 11 were untraded. Turnover rose to 280.8 million tolars from 279.5 million.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded share, easing 0.04 percent to 2,499 tolars on volume of 18,191 shares for a total turnover of 45.4 million tolars.
Brokerage Dadas led the day's decliners, tumbling 8.62 percent to 5,300 tolars on volume of 15 shares.
Traders said Dadas was one of the more speculative shares on the market and that the volume was too low to indicate an exact reason for such a fall.
Bank Dolenjska banka was the top gainer, jumping 4.34 percent to 14,920 tolars on volume of only five shares.

Brokers said the rise could have been partly due to the news two weeks ago that Daiwa Europe had been given the green light by the central bank to buy a 3.51 stake in the bank. However, they said volume was too low to really be able to judge the cause of the climb.
Petrol trader Petrol had the highest turnover, falling 5.37 percent to 18,850 tolars on volume of 3,857 shares for a total turnover of 74.5 million tolars. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
